clue.text: Clubs know how to proceed over strong drink

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: in a down-style reading 'over' tells us to turn the phrase before it backwards

parts.note: if you know how to proceed, you can go

explanation.surface: Someone at a card table works out their next move before ordering a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns CAN GO into OGNAC, which follows C for clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy from the Cognac region of France is a classic strong spirit.

clue.text: Protect from the sincerest flattery?

parts.note: imitation is said to be the sincerest flattery, and legal ownership of a work protects it against being imitated

explanation.surface: Someone wants to shield a person from being fawned over.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'imitation is the sincerest flattery' turns flattery into copying; the legal protection against copying is what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal right prevents others reproducing a work, guarding it against imitation.

clue.text: Nation seeing a danger in revolution

indicators.note: letters in revolution are turned over and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country is threatened by political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' rearranges A DANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island country in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Racecourse having a second function

parts.note: taken as written
cot is short for cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A racetrack doubles up as a venue for some other event.
explanation.walkthrough: COT is the cotangent, one of the trigonometric functions alongside sin and cos.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Man, perhaps putting work in, shortened the line on map

indicators.note: 'putting work in' places the work inside the island

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an isle
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before shortening

explanation.surface: A man, possibly working, cut short a line drawn on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man, perhaps' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man; 'putting ... in' inserts the work, and 'shortened' drops the final E of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopleth is a line on a map joining points of equal value, like an isobar.

clue.text: Staying up alone, single, sadly without female to drink wine

indicators.note: here 'without' means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the rest
sadly signals the word is treated badly, its letters jumbled

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone sits up late on their own, lonely and wishing for a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges SINGLE into SELING; 'without' means outside here, so those letters split as SEL...ING around the female, the drink and the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure that stays up with no external help is self-supporting, standing alone.

clue.text: Rip up root roughly in preparation of flowers

indicators.note: handling something roughly suggests its letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A gardener tears out a plant clumsily while making a flower arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges RIP UP ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a scented mixture of dried petals and flowers.

clue.text: Mouth a sort of English

definitions.meaning: the tidal mouth of a river where it meets the sea
the accent of the Thames area around London and Essex, named after the river's mouth

explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is the British name for the accent of south-east England along the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A river mouth is this tidal stretch, and the accent of south-east England takes the same name.

clue.text: Lift one in for the landlord

indicators.note: 'in' tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a host is a landlord at an inn
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Raise a glass, with one going in for the pub landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to raise or lift it, often with ropes.

clue.text: Being unhelpful, dealing with cask maker in the country

indicators.note: 'in' places the dealing and the cask maker inside the country

parts.note: a nation is a country
ON means about or dealing with
a cooper makes barrels and casks

explanation.surface: A barrel maker in the provinces refuses to help with business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing with' looks like part of the definition but supplies ON; the cask maker and ON sit just after the first letter of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to cooperate is the state of being unhelpful.

clue.text: Like the time when one was not yet in form

definitions.text: Like the time when one was not yet in form

parts.words: Like the time when one was not yet in form
parts.note: form is a class at school, so this describes the years before a child starts school, not being out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a period when they were not yet on top of their game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like fitness but is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes the years before a child begins formal schooling.

clue.text: Here's a piece for everyone

parts.note: a musical passage marked for the whole orchestra to play together, not a slice handed round

explanation.surface: Someone hands out a share of cake to all present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests a portion but is a passage of music; the Italian marking means 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical term for a passage played by all performers together.

clue.text: Arsenic slipped into crumble dish

indicators.note: the element is slipped inside the other word

parts.note: to rot is to decay or crumble
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: Poison was slipped into a crumble served as a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a dish of meat cooked in the oven.

clue.text: Act with US moon shot? One might now

definitions.text: Act with US moon shot? One might now

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Russian space traveller might these days take part in an American lunar mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges ACT US MOON; the whole clue also says a Russian space traveller might now join an American mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmonaut is a Russian astronaut, who after the Cold War might join an American mission.

clue.text: Insect, one gaining purchase after mostly firm hold

indicators.note: after means the shopper goes after the shortened hold
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a grasp is a firm hold
a shopper is one making a purchase

explanation.surface: An insect clings on firmly, finding a foothold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' suggests grip, matching 'hold', but here it means buying: a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: The grasshopper is a jumping insect.

clue.text: Fight with reserve where one sees cutting

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A brawl over a reservation where someone saw a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' means a press cutting, not a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapbook is an album where press cuttings are pasted in.

clue.text: River flowing around wood

indicators.note: the river's letters flow round, the first moving to the end

parts.note: the Wye is a river in Wales and England

explanation.surface: A river curves round a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing around' moves the W of WYE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Yew is a tree, and its timber is a wood.

clue.text: Defeated side initially cried after victory, suffering a blow

indicators.note: after places the following pieces after the victory

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of the words

parts.note: wept means cried

explanation.surface: The losing team broke down in tears after the other side's win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes D and S from 'Defeated side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something windswept has been battered by a strong wind, suffering a blow.

clue.text: Letter read out in support of leisure activity

indicators.note: read out means the letter is spoken, so we hear its name

parts.note: T is a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A letter is read out in favour of a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken name of the letter T; golf is the leisure activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf tee is a peg supporting the ball.

clue.text: Group that's surrounded opponents getting stuck once

parts.note: East and North are opponents at the bridge table
clave is an old past tense of cleave, meaning stuck

explanation.surface: A party under siege finds its rivals stuck long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge East-West play North-South, so E and N are opponents; 'once' marks an archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory or community surrounded by another.

clue.text: Persuasive speaker is right anti-heroic, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A convincing orator is in fact rather unheroic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges R and ANTI-HEROIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorician is a skilled orator.

clue.text: Lottery prize has cut women's time in office

indicators.note: has cut means the letter is removed

parts.note: winnings are what you win in a lottery
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A lottery win shortened women's time in work.
explanation.walkthrough: WINNINGS minus W.
explanation.definitionFit: An innings is a period of power or tenure, a term in office.

clue.text: Tony's chap turns out to be a yes-man

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Tony's friend proves to be a flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges TONYS CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns on superiors, always agreeing.

clue.text: Just like the Robinsons to have slightly less than smart son

indicators.note: slightly less means a letter is dropped from the end

parts.note: swish means smart or stylish

explanation.surface: A family is slightly less fashionable than their son.
explanation.walkthrough: The Robinsons are the Swiss Family Robinson of the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The family in The Swiss Family Robinson are from Switzerland.

clue.text: Slacks but sounds exhausted

definitions.meaning: breathes hard, as when worn out

explanation.definitionFit: The word means trousers and also gasps for breath when tired.

clue.text: Deposit put on a jacket

parts.note: to park something is to deposit it

explanation.surface: Someone puts down money and slips on a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket.

clue.text: State offering house to princess

parts.note: Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta heroine

explanation.surface: A country offers a home to a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offering house to princess' attaches HO after IDA, the princess of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Pacific Northwest, so it names a state by example.

clue.text: Starts off gig on for dance? Bliss for some

indicators.note: each of the four words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A party guest heads off to a dance in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' removes the first letters of gig, on, for and dance, leaving IG N OR ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'ignorance is bliss' means not knowing is happiness for some people.

clue.text: Yodel around mountain a way of passing the word

definitions.text: a way of passing the word

indicators.note: around means the singing surrounds the mountain

parts.note: to yodel is to sing
a peak is a mountain

explanation.surface: A singer yodels around an Alpine summit to spread the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking is talking, a way of communicating words.

clue.text: Fool taken in by wager for dog

indicators.note: taken in means the fool goes inside the wager

parts.note: a bet is a wager
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool is conned by a bet on a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like conned but signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound breed.
